assumptions: Neighbors have no natural ordering, so aggregation should work on an unordered set.
For Theorem 1, feature vectors of different nodes must be separated by more than a fixed constant C.
guarantees: Can approximate node clustering coefficients after K = 4 iterations under the theorem assumptions.
Outperforms strong baselines on three inductive node-classification benchmarks.
Can classify unseen nodes and generalize to unseen graphs.
formalism.operation: GraphSAGE aggregates neighbor information, combines it with the node's own information, and uses a neural network layer to get the new node representation.

evidence_spans.objects: Graph G(V, E); input features {xᵥ, ∀v ∈ V}
evidence_spans.assumptions: a node's neighbors have no natural ordering
